summary: BLM lookout at Lazy Mountain, Matanuska-Susitna Borough, was manned in 1970 per the BLM Alaska fire report; no source gives its build date, fate or remains.

facts.agency: Bureau of Land Management, Alaska State Office (per the 1970 Alaska Fire Report)
facts.status_note: No source after 1970 says whether a lookout stood on the summit, was removed or survives; sources describe the summit trail only

access.note: The summit is reached by a public hiking trail in a Mat-Su Borough park; no source describes the lookout site itself

visit.trail_note: About 2.2-mile hiking trail; the first mile is steep and unmaintained; check the Mat-Su Borough website for closures, especially in spring and early summer

events.note: Listed among the Anchorage-Palmer area sites where lookouts were manned in 1970

notes_for_editor: The only source for the lookout is one sentence in the 1970 BLM Alaska Fire Report, which says the Bureau 'manned' lookouts at 'Lazy Mountain' among sites in the Anchorage-Palmer area. The report does not say the Lazy Mountain site was a tower, so kind stays unknown, and it names a summit, not a tower position: the GNIS point (61.62271, -148.96616) is approximate. The brief's record lists the agency as BLM; the summit is now a Mat-Su Borough park trail, so any land-ownership change since 1970 is not documented here. No build date, design, removal or remains are documented. Not checked: Matanuska Valley and Palmer newspaper archives, BLM Alaska Fire Service records. No photo found; no NHLR or FFLOS record found.
